answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with identity-bound, exponentially priced throughput quotas. Each verified identity gets a small free quota; extra capacity must be bought with tokens locked as a bond, and the price doubles with every additional tier, so a tide of fakes becomes unaffordable. Honest agents build a signal of reliability from peer-checked work, keeping them at the base rate, while misbehavior burns the bond. At the nadir of an attack, when fakes compete for scarce quota, their marginal cost keeps rising, so flooding costs far more than any gain from extra votes.
